messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details:
The failure occurs in the method WordUtils.abbreviate(String str, int lower, int upper, String appendToEnd). According to the bug report and code inspection:

- The method adjusts the 'upper' parameter to be at most the length of the string if 'upper' is -1 or greater than the string length (lines 618-620).
- Then, if 'upper' is less than 'lower', it raises 'upper' to be equal to 'lower' (lines 621-624).
- However, the 'lower' parameter itself is never capped to the string length.
  
Because of this, if 'lower' is greater than the string length, 'upper' is adjusted to 'lower' (which is > string length), causing 'upper' to be set beyond the string length. Then in the substring call at line 629 (str.substring(0, upper)) or line 635 (str.substring(0, upper)), a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException is thrown because upper exceeds the valid substring range.

The test example also highlights the scenario where lower > str.length(). The missing check/fix is on the 'lower' parameter to cap it at the string's length before applying other adjustments.

In short, the root cause is that 'lower' is not limited to the length of the string; subsequent adjustments based on 'lower' cause 'upper' to go out of bounds, leading to the exception.

This aligns exactly with the bug report's description and demonstrates why the failure occurs. The fix should involve adding a step to cap 'lower' at str.length() before modifying 'upper' or other logic.

This explains the cause of the test failure and how the exception occurs while invoking substrings beyond string length.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
